agentHost: support MCP sampling requests

- Use the Copilot SDK to run approved MCP sampling requests.
- Show live sampling requests as tool calls with confirmation controls.
- Save server sampling approvals in host settings for all sessions.
- Show prompt character counts instead of prompt contents.
- Cancel pending sampling when a request completes or the chat stops.
- Add tests for approval, persistence, cancellation, and UI routing.
- Update the sampling E2E test to decline the new confirmation.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/340796

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed event callback is fire-and-forget, the execution call is directly awaited only inside each independent handler, no limiter/sequencer wraps it, and the added tests explicitly establish concurrent requests with independent confirmations. The SDK boundary is documented in the changed code as owning model selection and inference; only the number of servers that issue bursts is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Concurrent SDK model-inference RPCs and their retained pending request objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With N simultaneous `sampling.requested` events from approved servers, the host starts N inference RPCs and retains N pending executions; there is no session-wide or per-server upper bound.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded concurrent model traffic can saturate provider capacity, reduce throughput through throttling, and delay the foreground chat turn.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, server-initiated `sampling.requested` events were immediately rejected through `handlePendingSampling`; they never crossed the `executeSampling` inference boundary, regardless of request concurrency.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each approved request, and every request from a host-approved server, immediately starts its own SDK sampling execution. `_pendingMcpSamplings` only tracks IDs for cancellation and does not bound active work.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 5515 invokes `_executeMcpSampling` independently from every `sampling.requested` handler; the same diff registers the event with `void this._handleSamplingRequest(e.data)`, so handlers are not awaited or queued. Previously this event called `_rejectSamplingRequest`, which performed no sampling execution.
Findings.Title: Bound concurrent sampling executions
Findings.Impact: After a user selects “Always Allow,” an MCP server that submits a batch of sampling requests can start all model inferences at once. Those calls contend with the active chat for provider/network capacity, causing throttling and increased turn latency; a larger burst also accumulates pending request state until every inference finishes.
Findings.Evidence: `onSamplingRequested` launches `_handleSamplingRequest` without awaiting it; after approval, line 5515 calls `_executeMcpSampling`, whose implementation immediately calls `this._wrapper.session.rpc.mcp.executeSampling`. The only shared structure is an unbounded `Set`. The added `concurrent requests have independent tool confirmations` test demonstrates that multiple sampling handlers coexist, while host-wide approval removes the only user-paced gate. Existing subsystem code uses `Limiter` for other fan-out boundaries, but this path has none.
Findings.Recommendation: Route server-initiated sampling through a disposable session-level (or per-server plus global) limiter with a small explicit concurrency cap, preserving cancellation while queued; reject or bound excess queued requests so a server cannot grow pending state indefinitely.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive or preapproved server-initiated MCP sampling
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SDK `sampling.requested` event → validate/count request → identify server/read approval → emit start/ready UI state → wait for user approval when needed → `rpc.mcp.executeSampling` model inference → `rpc.ui.handlePendingSampling` response. Model inference and the final SDK response are on the server request's critical path; UI confirmation is additionally on the cold/unapproved path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke SDK sampling, which owns model selection and inference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model-inference RPC per approved sampling request; N simultaneous approved requests produce N calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Server-originated sampling events were rejected and made zero inference calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request cannot resolve until inference completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish synthetic tool-call state through the agent-host protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two initial actions and one completion action per surfaced request, delivered to subscribed chat clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Rejected sampling events emitted no synthetic tool-call actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The ready action is required before interactive approval; completion follows inference.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve `handlePendingSampling`, optionally with the model response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK control response per incoming request, whether approved or rejected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary was called once per event, always without a response to reject it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes the original server request after inference or denial.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number N of concurrent `sampling.requested` events, especially from a server whose identity has host-wide approval.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each event starts an independent async handler. Unapproved calls are user-paced but multiple confirmations can remain pending; after approval, executions have no limiter and can overlap without bound.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The host reads the approval list from in-memory root state on every request and recomputes the server fingerprint; there is no sampling-result cache or request coalescing. A cold unapproved identity waits for confirmation; a warm approved identity skips that wait.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: fire-and-forget event dispatch, independent handlers, direct inference RPCs, and absence of a limiter are all explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often real MCP servers issue concurrent sampling requests is uncertain, but the approved path has no host-side cap and protocol requests can coexist, as the added concurrent-request test demonstrates.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity concurrency burst: after approval, N events immediately produce N expensive model calls and N retained pending executions.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: User chooses “Always Allow” → synchronous root-state update → sampling proceeds. The queued filesystem persistence is launched without awaiting it, so disk completion is off the sampling critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize root configuration and write the host config file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one filesystem write for each newly approved server identity, rewriting the root config file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No sampling approval setting was persisted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the sampling critical path because `updateRootConfig` does not await persistence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct server identities the user permanently approves.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Root-config file writes are serialized by `_rootConfigWrite`; concurrent approvals for the same identity observe the synchronously updated state and avoid duplicate writes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Approval identity is persisted once and subsequently read from in-memory root config; duplicate identities avoid another write. There is no negative cache beyond absence from the list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the write path and its off-critical-path placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The root configuration's total size varies, but approvals are explicit user actions and writes are serialized and deduplicated by identity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: writes are user-paced, deduplicated, serialized, and off the inference critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Publishing successful sampling results in chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Inference result → resolve original SDK request → stringify result for the tool completion → dispatch/store completion. Serialization occurs synchronously before completion publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Pretty-print the full sampling response into text content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full JSON serialization and one chat action per successful sampling response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Server sampling was rejected, so no response was serialized into chat state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous serialization precedes UI completion; the action is then published to clients and retained in the turn state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Successful response byte size and number of sampling calls retained in a turn/history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialization occurs independently in every sampling handler and therefore can overlap across a burst, though each individual stringify is synchronous on the event loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache is used; every approved request returns a fresh model response. The completion action retains a formatted copy in chat state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the copy is made and retained; lower confidence that realistic individual response sizes alone create material degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal response sizes are bounded in practice by the server's requested token limit, and repository evidence does not establish commonly large outputs; this kept the concern below the reporting threshold as a separate issue.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the allocation mechanism is real but material impact beyond the reported burst is not sufficiently established.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat abort, session disposal, or SDK `sampling.completed` → cancel token and issue `cancelSamplingExecution` for active executions. Cleanup is not required to await remote cancellation before the chat stops.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel model sampling executions in the SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK cancellation RPC per active sampling execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Server sampling created no executions to cancel; direct MCP App executions were already tracked and cancelled on teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Best-effort and not awaited during teardown; it does not block chat cancellation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active executions at abort/disposal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cancellation RPCs are launched in parallel, one per active execution; their cardinality is inherited from the unbounded execution burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Pending IDs are tracked in sets/maps only for ownership and cancellation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: disposal map, linked cancellation tokens, and cancellation RPC paths are explicit and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote cancellation duration is irrelevant to teardown latency because calls are not awaited; burst cardinality remains covered by the concurrency finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate cleanup finding: ownership and late-result suppression are present; cancellation fan-out is a consequence of the reported unbounded execution fan-out.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: MCP App `sampling/createMessage` → `rpc.mcp.executeSampling` → return SDK result. The PR adds cancellation racing/tracking around the existing boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute model sampling for an MCP App request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK/model sampling call per MCP App request, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old implementation already called `rpc.mcp.executeSampling` once per request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Inference remains on the request's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of direct MCP App sampling requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: As before, direct App requests may overlap; the diff does not increase their call count or move them onto a new path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caching or coalescing is introduced; each MCP App request remains a distinct SDK sampling operation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that this is a refactor plus improved cancellation, not a new performance cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: App request frequency is unknown, but PR causality for additional work is absent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: expensive-boundary cardinality is unchanged and cancellation is better bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files. One introduced issue was submitted: server-originated sampling handlers can fan out into unbounded concurrent model inference after host approval. Approval persistence, result serialization, cancellation, UI routing, and the pre-existing MCP App path were traced without additional high-confidence reportable regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
